paragraphs: Companies adopted open-plan offices on the theory that removing walls would encourage spontaneous conversation and thus innovation. Several studies suggest the opposite effect. When two firms that had moved to open layouts were observed, face-to-face interaction fell by roughly two-thirds, and employees compensated by sending more email. A likely explanation is that people who feel watched by colleagues withdraw, using headphones as a kind of portable wall. Some managers dismiss these findings as the product of workers' resistance to change, but the studies were carried out months after the move, long enough for novelty and irritation to have faded. Open plans do reduce the cost of floor space, which may be the real reason for their popularity.
